papers.title: Local wild mapping class groups and cabled braids
papers.abstract: We will define and study some generalisations of pure $\mathfrak{g}$-braid groups that occur in the theory of connections on curves, for any complex reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. They make up local pieces of the wild mapping class groups, which are fundamental groups of (universal) deformations of wild Riemann surfaces, underlying the braiding of Stokes data and generalising the usual mapping class groups. We will establish a general product decomposition for the local wild mapping class groups, and in many cases define a fission tree controlling this decomposition. Further in type A we will show one obtains cabled versions of braid groups, related to braid operads.

papers.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
papers.abstract: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.

papers.title: An Unexpected Rational Blowdown
papers.abstract: The rational blowdown operation in 4-manifold topology replaces a neighborhood of a configuration of spheres by a rational homology ball. Such configurations typically arise from resolutions of surface singularities that admit rational homology disk smoothings. Conjecturally, all such singularities must be weighted homogeneous and belong to certain specific families: Stipsicz-Szab\'o--Wahl constructed QHD smoothings for these families and used Donaldson's theorem to obtain very restrictive necessary conditions on the resolution graphs for singularities with this property. In particular, these results, as well as subsequent work of Bhupal-Stipsicz, show that for certain resolution graphs, the canonical contact structure on the link of the singularity cannot admit a QHD symplectic filling. By contrast, we exhibit Stein rational homology disk fillings for the contact links of an infinite family of rational singularities that are not weighted homogeneous, producing a new symplectic rational blowdown. Inspiration for our construction comes from de Jong-van Straten's description of Milnor fibers of sandwiched singularities; we use the symplectic analog of de Jong-van Straten theory developed by the second and third authors. The unexpected Stein fillings are built using spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations.

papers.title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
papers.abstract: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.

papers.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vign\'eras
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vign\'eras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.

papers.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
papers.abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

papers.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
papers.abstract: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth M\"obius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

papers.title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
papers.abstract: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Sch\"utz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

papers.title: A short proof of the universality of the fundamental shadow links
papers.abstract: We give a constructive three-dimensional proof of Costantino and Thurston's universality theorem for fundamental shadow links. More precisely, every compact connected oriented three-manifold with empty or toroidal boundary can be obtained by integral Dehn filling along a subset of the boundary components of a fundamental shadow link exterior.

papers.title: Loop Space Models and Integral Homology of Connected Quandles
papers.abstract: We construct a marked integral delooping of a connected quandle's covering monoid, realizing its rack space as a homotopy fiber. For finite connected quandles at primes $p$ not dividing a point-stabilizer order, we determine the local $A_\infty$ type and the ordinary rack cohomology shuffle algebra over fields of characteristic $p$. We compute integral quandle homology in all positive degrees for finite connected regular cyclic Alexander quandles and the tetrahedral quandle. At such primes dividing the quandle order, rack-space homotopy groups have exponentially many cyclic direct summands of fixed $p$-power order in each sufficiently large degree.

papers.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
papers.abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ there exists a finite generating set $A$ such that $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;A)$ is contractible for all $t\ge 1$. We prove this as a special case of a more general result about certain groups. Let $G$ be a group and $H$ a subgroup. A subgroup $F\le G$ is a supplement of $H$ in $G$ if $G=HF$. We prove that for $H\le G$ with $F$ a supplement of $H$ in $G$, for generating sets $A_H$ and $A_G$ of $H$ and $G$ satisfying certain conditions involving $F$, the Vietoris-Rips complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;A_G)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A_H)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$. In particular this applies to affine Coxeter groups, since free abelian groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. Beyond these general results, we also investigate affine Coxeter groups $W_a$ specifically using the standard generating set $S$, and prove contractibility of $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ for large enough $t$.

papers.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
papers.abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

papers.title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
papers.abstract: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

papers.title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $\Sigma_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $\Sigma_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

papers.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
papers.abstract: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.

papers.title: Higher order unknotting numbers for knots and links
papers.abstract: Ohyama, Taniyama and Yamada showed that finite type knot invariants are insensitive to the unknotting number: for any integer n and any knot K, there is an unknotting number 1 knot which cannot be distinguished from K by any finite type invariant of order $\le n$. We generalize this result in three directions. First, we prove an analogous result for all higher order unknotting number given by $C_n$-moves. Second, we give several extensions to the link case. Third, we show that a similar result holds for ribbon 2-knots.

papers.title: The Torelli Group and Euler Class Zero $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Representations
papers.abstract: We prove that every representation of a closed surface group of genus at least $3$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ that is sufficiently close (but not equal to) a representation that has non-compact solvable image has a simple closed separating curve that is mapped to a non-trivial elliptic element in $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. This can be seen as evidence for an affirmative answer to a question of Bowditch and a conjecture of Goldman.

papers.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
papers.abstract: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.

papers.title: Gluons and Knots
papers.abstract: We argue that the scattering amplitude of a single minus helicity gluon with arbitrarily many positive helicity gluons is topological. The amplitude is constant in chambers of kinematic space, its resonances are located at walls and its factorization is determined by wall-crossing. Yangian invariance dictates the amplitude to be determined by a 2d null Wilson loop that can be lifted into a positive and transverse 3d link. By reinterpreting wall-crossing and the Weinberg soft theorem as skein relations and Reidemeister moves of the subknots, we construct a state-counting description consisting of adding the `corners' of their HOMFLY-PT polynomials. Beyond the classical limit, we argue that this provides a conjectured but precise connection to topological field and string theory. The new formula is rigorously derived via a Lean-formalized dependency graph (DAG) as detailed in a companion paper, laying out the precise assumptions including Reidemeister III invariance. It is further tested exhaustively, including novel `star' kinematics where the amplitude and state count are shown to become Catalan numbers, in agreement with knot theory literature.

papers.title: Topology of irregular isomonodromy times on a fixed pointed curve
papers.abstract: We will define and study (moduli) spaces of deformations of irregular classes on Riemann surfaces, which provide an intrinsic viewpoint on the `times' of irregular isomonodromy systems in general. Our aim is to study the deeper generalisation of the G-braid groups that occur as fundamental groups of such deformation spaces, with particular focus on the generalisation of the full G-braid groups.

papers.title: A generalization of the Perelman gluing theorem and applications
papers.abstract: We extend a positive Ricci curvature gluing theorem of Perelman to a range of positive intermediate curvature conditions, ranging from positive scalar curvature up to (and including) positive sectional curvature. As an application of this, we demonstrate that the observer moduli space of metrics with positive intermediate Ricci curvatures can have non-trivial higher homotopy groups. Further applications include deriving a sufficient condition for the existence of a metric with positive intermediate Ricci curvature and totally geodesic boundary.

papers.title: Categorical Tiling Theory: Constructing Directed Planar Tilings via Edge Reversal
papers.abstract: Tilings of the plane resemble the simplicial and other complexes from algebraic topology, but have not been studied from this perspective. We construct finite categories corresponding to polygons with labeled directed edges, and introduce the problem of modeling tilings of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane as presheaves over such a category. Combinatorially, this amounts to choosing an ``alignment'' for a tiling: a direction for every edge and consistent labels for the edges of each polygonal tile. We show that for a fixed tiling, given a single alignment we can characterize every other alignment of the same tiling by comparison of the edge directions. We then construct a ``reflective'' alignment for any tiling with an even number of polygons at each vertex, and from this generate a large family of alignments with elegant symmetry properties.

papers.title: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
papers.abstract: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_{\Gamma}/Z(A_{\Gamma})$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.

papers.title: Links and singularities of stable maps from $3$-manifolds to surfaces
papers.abstract: For any two links in the $3$-sphere, we provide a visual construction of a stable map $f$ from the $3$-sphere to the Euclidean plane such that $f$ has no cusp points, the set of definite (resp. indefinite) fold points of $f$ is isotopic to the first (resp. second) given link, and $f$ does not have a certain type of singular fibers. Moreover, we obtain a similar result for any $3$-manifold by setting the target space to the $2$-sphere.

papers.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
papers.abstract: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.

papers.title: Smallest quotients and profinite rigidity of irreducible spherical type Artin groups
papers.abstract: We prove that irreducible spherical type Artin groups are profinitely rigid within the class of all spherical type Artin groups. As part of the proof, building on ideas of Kolay for the $n$-strand braid group, we compute the smallest non-abelian quotient of every spherical type Artin group. In particular, given an irreducible spherical type Artin group, its smallest non-abelian quotient is always that of the corresponding Coxeter group, except for dihedral Artin groups of weight divisible by $4$, which all have $\mathfrak S_3$ as a non-abelian quotient. Parts of the proof also rely on the computation of the cohomological dimension of the profinite completion of certain Artin groups.

papers.title: Sections, pseudosections, and multisections of Lefschetz fibrations
papers.abstract: We show that not every symplectic Lefschetz fibration over the $2$--sphere admits a smooth section, settling a long-standing open problem. To prove this, we develop a method for studying sections via lifts of monodromy factorizations with point-pushing maps and the induced handle decomposition of the total space, and apply it to an infinite family of Lefschetz fibrations. In contrast, we show that every Lefschetz fibration over $S^2$ admits positive multisections. Some of these examples admit no multisections with spherical components. We also construct signature-zero Lefschetz fibrations of every odd genus $g\geq 7$, which in turn give symplectic Lefschetz fibrations of any prescribed signature in each of these genera.
